result:
## Final Report

**Lightest all-PASS design found: 2 mm graphite, 3.6 kg/m²** — appeared at evaluation 6 (of 7 transports used; 7/12 budget spent, 10/40 screens).

Full margins on the winning design: screen 401K (pass, margin 19K), hotspot 335K (pass, margin 4.69K vs 340K limit), mass 3.6 kg/m² (pass, margin 96.4 kg), thickness 2mm (pass, margin 3.8cm).

**Path to the result:** The prior campaign's best was 10mm graphite at 18 kg/m². The constellation showed hotspot temperature staying flat (~324-325K) across 10-30mm for both aluminium and graphite, suggesting convective resistance — not lateral spreading — dominated in that range, so I tested much thinner graphite. This paid off: 3mm, 5mm, 8mm graphite all passed with large margins, and bisection found the real boundary between 1mm (fails, hotspot 344K) and 2mm (passes, hotspot 335K). I also tested whether higher-conductivity materials (aluminium k=200, aluminium_nitride k=170) could pass at the 1mm floor and beat 2mm graphite's mass — both failed (aluminium came very close, -0.193K margin), and copper would pass at 1mm but at 8.96 kg/m² is already heavier than the winner.

I stopped rather than spend the remaining 5 transports because the physics is airtight: 1mm is the minimum whole-mm layer thickness, any multi-layer design needs ≥2mm total, graphite has the lowest density of any material with usable conductivity, and 2mm pure graphite already passes — so nothing in the material table can beat 3.6 kg/m² without violating either the thickness floor or the hotspot limit.

**What I'd try next with more budget:** test whether a very thin high-conductivity cap (e.g., 1mm copper or aluminium) over 1mm graphite could pass at 2mm total with a comfortable margin as a lower-risk alternative (though it would be heavier than pure graphite, so not useful for minimizing mass, only for margin/robustness trade-offs); or explore mass safety margin at 2mm graphite under material-property uncertainty, since the current margin (4.69K) is real but tighter than 3-8mm alternatives.
